Careers Education
On 3rd March we partnered with Canterbury Academy to hold our annual "next steps" post 16 progression fair. 9 providers of post 16 courses for students with EHCP, plus Kent Supported Employment, came to meet our pupils and explain what they have to offer to help them on their path to employment once they leave school.
Here is a video of some past St Nicholas students speaking about their experience of the school at an NHS conference.
All Oak pathway classes from year 7 to year 10 were able to go along and start to form an idea of where they might like to go once their time with us finishes- pupils will have visited all these providers by the end of year 10 so should be able to make the right choice. We are very grateful to all these organisations who gave their time to meet our pupils; Liberty Training; Supajam; Brogdale; Beacon Plus; Canterbury Academy 6 Plus; Kent Supported Employment; Bemix; Lily's Bistro & Social Kitchen; East Kent College; and KITE College.

Creative Therapies Team
We are a group of counsellors and therapists at St Nicholas School. We offer a range of therapy programmes tailored to the child’s needs and provide a safe, therapeutic space for our students.
Creative Therapies Team
Creative therapies can be helpful to any child or young person who finds it difficult to express their thoughts and feelings verbally. They may also help with addressing painful feelings or experiences, including experiences of trauma. It can help to identify new strategies for managing feelings, thoughts, and behaviours. Our role is to facilitate the expression of the young person’s thoughts and emotions through creative means. They can build resilience and reduce anxiety in the young person, providing encouragement and support to the young person, their parents, caregivers, and teachers throughout the journey of fostering positive transformation.

The Governors
Introduction to the Governing Body
The dynamic, dedicated and experienced board of governors at St Nicholas School supports the school in a number of ways. It provides strategic leadership and accountability, appoints the Head Teacher and Deputy Headteachers, and ensures the schools performance is continually monitored, evaluated and improved.
It is governors who hold the main responsibility for the school’s finances, and it is governors who work with the headteacher to make the best use of the money we receive. They are also ultimately responsible for important matters such as teaching and learning, safeguarding, health and safety, staffing and premises.
Visible Governance campaign | National Governance Association
The board comprises governors elected by parents, appointed on the basis of their skills and experience, and appointed by the Local Authority. Together they work hard to support the Head Teacher, staff and pupils with the aim of ensuring that St Nicholas School is the best it can be and provides the highest quality education for our children and young people.
Minutes of FGB meetings can be obtained by request from the school office. This does not include any confidential minutes.
Governors
Sharon Godden
Sharon brings a strong background in financial markets, with expertise in strategic planning and bespoke financial solutions. She has applied her professional and analytical skills in a variety of education and health-related settings, with a long-standing commitment to supporting children with complex needs. Sharon has served on the governing body of St Nicholas School for many years, including key leadership roles such as Vice Chair, Chair of the Finance and Resources Committee, and Interim Chair of Governors before stepping into the role of Chair. She was also a parent ambassador on the Department for Education-funded Complex Learning Difficulties and Disabilities Research Project. She is currently a member of the Advisory Council of the charity Together for Short Lives and is actively involved in children’s health and palliative care through her current role as Commissioning and Partnerships Manager at Demelza Hospice Care for Children. Sharon’s work connects her with NHS and Local Authority partners across Kent and Medway, South East London and East Sussex. She enjoys hockey, running, cycling, and Pilates.
Angela Pike
Angela graduated from The University of East Anglia in 1982 with a teaching degree and a focus on Special Educational Needs. Her first teaching role was in a post 16 unit for young people with complex physical and health needs in London. Following this Angela spent three years in a residential school in Berkshire for children with a wide range of learning and emotional needs. Angela started her life at St Nicholas in 1987 as teacher in the Reception class and then went on to be phase manager for the Primary department. In the year 2000 Angela was appointed Deputy Head Teacher at the school. She went on to lead on many projects including the training of new teachers and support of children in mainstream schools with SEN. She retired in the summer of 2017 and after many happy years at the school, was asked to become a governor and is now only too happy to continue to support the school and the pupils in any way possible. Angela has two grown up children and enjoys a very outdoor life which includes dog walking!
Penny Webb
Penny is a Senior Lecturer at Canterbury Christ Church University in Primary Education and leads Special Educational Needs (SEN) and Inclusion for the Primary department. Before joining Christ Church in 2016, Penny worked as primary school teacher for 22 years and started her career in a special school. As a teacher, Penny took on a range of leadership roles, including History and Geography, Literacy, RE and SENCo. Now, Penny teaches students about teaching and supporting children with SEN. She owns a Dunkirk little ship, is member of the Association of Dunkirk Little Ships and loves to get out on the water whenever she can.
Jesse Sazant
Jesse is the Chief Operating Officer of The Canterbury Academy Trust. He has been a school leader at both primary and secondary level, having taught from, Year 1 through to Year 13 in a variety of subjects. He is passionate about education being a vehicle to support each and every young person in pursuing their dreams. Outside of work, basketball coaching is his passion and he is currently Programme Lead for GB Maxibasketball.
Joe White
Joe is Deputy Principal of Meadowfield School in Kent. He has spent his career in special education including a working in a residential special school. Joe is a Principal Instructor for the Kent PROACT SCIPr UK® Network where he works closely with colleagues to develop Proactive behaviour support in schools. He runs the website inclusiveteach.com which shares free SEN teaching resources and sensory stories.
Emma Wellard
I've been working at St Nicholas School since 1996, firstly as a T.A, then HLTA and furthered my training by completing an Integrative Counselling diploma in 2013. I have since trained as a clinical supervisor and Level 5/6 CYP counsellor. I am lucky enough to lead the St Nicholas well-being team, designated mental health lead and train in areas such as Proact Scip, Solihull two-day foundation and reflective supervision. I am also wife to Adrian and Mum to Bena and Abby. I care for my father.. and I do have time for other things! which includes chairperson of my local allotments, working my two allotment plots and gardening. I enjoy my role as staff governor as it gives me a greater understanding of the processes and structures of running a Special School.
Emma Blackmore
Emma is a Deputy Headteacher in a mainstream primary school in Ashford. She has been working in education for over 20 years and in Senior Leadership since 2016. Emma currently leads Behaviour and Personal development within the school she works for and is also a Designated Safeguarding Lead. Emma has experience of teaching from Reception up to Year 6, with a majority of her time spent within Key Stage One. Emma's son has attended St Nicholas School since the start of Reception and is on the Beech Pathway.
Melanie Judi
Melanie brings to the Governing Body a wealth of experience from her long and dedicated career in secondary education. A specialist in French and Spanish, she has taught across a range of year groups and held several key leadership roles, including Head of Department, Head of Careers, and Boarding Houseparent. Having completed her MA in 2024, Melanie is eager to apply her knowledge of educational leadership to support the continued development of the school. She is particularly passionate about contributing to the careers education of pupils and offering guidance to the teaching team wherever it may be helpful.
Frankie Watts
I have two children who attend St Nicholas School and have been a part of the school for 4 years now. I currently serve as Chair of the PTFA since 2025 a role I really enjoy. I am passionate about supporting the school through fundraising and helping to organise events that benefit all the children. I took on the role of Parent Governor from last year as I care deeply about the school and want to contribute further to its continued success.

Language and Communication Support
Speech, Language and Communication Needs
The school work closely with the local NHS Speech and language therapy team to provide a skilled workforce to support your child with their speech, language and communication needs.
Some pupils may receive input from a specific SaLT, but many will benefit from the wide range of skills, knowledge and interventions from their teachers and class staff. This will include interventions such as Intensive Interaction, Makaton, Language through Colour, Clicker 8, Communicate in Print, Cued Articulation, GRID player and many varied visual supports amongst some.
The school is also working alongside local professionals and practitioners on the ‘Balanced System’ . This is a system to evidence the work we consistently do with the pupils. It helps us to identify where there is a need, and what interventions can be implemented and to show where we can offer training and support to skill our workforce. It also demonstrates how we work with our families to bridge the gap with home, ensuring that your child makes the best progress with their SLCN needs.
To find out more about this system, please follow the link below. www.thebalancedsystem.org
We have also included a parent brochure to help parents and carers support their child at home with their SLCN needs. If you would like more support with supporting your child at home, please ask your child’s teacher.

SOLIHULL APPROACH
Solihull have released a new course "Understanding Your Child with Additional Needs". It is a substantial course, similar to "Understanding Your Child" but it has been rewritten for parents of children with additional needs.
Solihull have created a Feedback Widget for each Unit and would welcome any feedback especially as this is a new course.
This online course is for parents with a child with additional needs. It is for parents, relatives and friends of children who may have a physical or learning disability or who may have autistic traits. In the UK, you may be within the SEND (Special educational needs and disability) system. Some parents describe their child as differently abled, or neuroatypical.
This course is in two sections:
• Level 1 lays the foundation for understanding your child
• Level 2 looks at some particular aspects of parenting: sleeping and anger management, together with more about how we interact with each other.
Understanding this can make it easier to work with your child's behaviour as well as supporting their development. Once you finish Level 1 you can progress to Level 2 if you'd like to. You can print off a certificate at the end of the course as well as one at the end of Level 1.
All courses are available here: https://www.inourplace.co.uk

Online Safety
Online Safety is given the highest priority at St. Nicholas School.
We have a regular ongoing programme of Online Safety training for staff and students. Workshops are offered to parents throughout the year, that offer advice which is not only relevant to the young people at St. Nicholas School, but also to their siblings and adults in this changing online and digital world we live in.
Please keep an eye on the News and Events section to see when the next parents workshop is taking place and for the monthly online safety bulletins.
If you have an Online Safety concern, please contact Stephen King (Deputy Head) at s.king@stns.org.uk or Dave Jenner (Assistant Headteacher) at d.jenner@stns.org.uk .
Alternatively for more information please check out any of these recommended sources of advice.

Home Learning - STLS
From September, we will be making a small but important change to how manage chew toys in school. Whilst many children already come into school with chew toys we need to share that we have designed, with support from Kent County Council (Health and Safety) some monitoring forms to help ensure that all items sent in are safe and fit for purpose.
Some chew toy items that are purchased from less-reputable sources, have the potential to contain internal parts, may contain toxic material, break up more easily and / or have strain chains without a breakable snap clap. These items are not always safe as they can present a choking risk or could get caught / snagged leading to them pulling tightly around the neck.
We need to ensure that the items that are sent in:
• Are purchased from a reputable source
• Are age and stage appropriate
• Have no internal parts • Has a working breakable clasp
• Is in a good condition
We already make daily informal visual checks on any items sent in from home, but starting from September we will make a formal inspection of chewing items once per term. This will sit alongside the daily checks.
